# Baize -- equivalence evidence (step 4 of the migration protocol)

Collected 2026-08-09 with BOTH launchers present and the old one canonical, per AC-11.18. Every sealed comparison cites the seal path from its run's `verdict:` line, never a dereferenced `LATEST_*` (the two suffix families share those pointer names -- and the old and new runs of minute 1859 demonstrate why: the new run took the `-SS` collision suffix and re-pointed the shared LATEST). Runs were strictly sequential -- the launchers share `_build` and `tmp/`.

## The examines table

| Gate            | Old (`bin/baize`)                                          | New (`bin/devbin`)                                         | Verdict                        |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| test mix        | rc 0; `Result: 29 passed` (suite marker -- runs are SUITE-SCOPED both sides; the bare full suite is forbidden by the standing rule the runner itself enforces); seal `20260809-1859.mix.errors` 0 bytes | rc 0; SAME Result line verbatim, same 29 glyphs; seal `20260809-1901.MIX.errors` 0 bytes | IDENTICAL counts, both sealed  |
| test credo      | rc 0 (seal empty = completed green); `Checking 330 source files`; `1908 mods/funs, found no issues.`; seal `20260809-1859.credo.errors` 0 bytes | rc 0; SAME two lines verbatim; seal `20260809-1859-35.CREDO.errors` 0 bytes | IDENTICAL examined set         |
| test shell      | rc 0; `assert_test.sh: ok (18 assertions)` + `helpers_test.sh: ok (46 assertions)` | rc 0; SAME two lines; the run_suite sentinel contract (`BAIZE_SHELL_SENTINEL_DIR`) held under the new runner | IDENTICAL, deliberately unsealed both sides |
| test rust       | rc 3, the not_yet stub text                                | rc 3, BYTE-IDENTICAL stub text                             | stub preserved                 |
| test all        | rc 0; mix-skipped notice; `skipped (stub, not run): rust`; `all gates passed` | rc 0; all three lines IDENTICAL                            | same aggregation, same buckets |
| check compile   | rc 0 (inside check all; rack-scoped subprocess, --warnings-as-errors --force) | rc 0 via `cmd/.lib/check-compile` -- same cd, same flags, sealed under tmp/check/ | same enforcement scope         |
| check format    | rc 0 (`mix format --check-formatted`)                      | rc 0, one arm (elixir; shell has no fmt arm)               | same command, same verdict     |
| check deps      | rc 0                                                       | rc 0, sealed empty                                         | same command, same verdict     |
| check toolchain | rc 0; pins 1.20.3 / 29.0.5 == active (GREEN -- the sweep was a verified no-op, AC-11.17; no image arm exists to pair red on) | rc 0; `elixir 1.20.3` + `erlang 29.0.5`                    | same facts, same verdict       |
| check critic    | rc 0; runs elixir, swift, rust, shell (the intent-config x headless intersection) | rc 0; the SAME four languages -- critic reads the Intent declaration directly, so devbin's `[elixir, shell]` activation key does not narrow it | same dispatch, same honesty    |
| check credo     | rc 0, delegates to the sealed runner                       | rc 0, same delegation via `cmd/.lib/check-credo` (plus a tmp/check seal -- the devbin norm) | one `mix credo` home, both sides |
| check all       | rc 0 over six gates (order: toolchain format deps compile critic credo) | rc 0 over the SAME six (order: compile credo format deps toolchain critic -- declared rows first, then catalogue) | same coverage; order owned below |

**The promotion pairs.** A bogus path (`apps/rack/test/no/such/path_test.exs`): rc 1 BOTH sides with `PROMOTED TO FAILED` in both logs -- Baize originated this rule and the port keeps it. `--allow-empty`: rc 0 both sides. `--env dev` into test mix: rc 1 both sides with the byte-identical refusal `baize: test mix runs under MIX_ENV=test (got 'dev')`.

## Byte-identical probes

`diff` clean, old vs new: `version` (bare), `-v`, `version show`, **`which`** (the full PATH-walk report -- the whole ported command, output-identical), unknown command (rc 2 both), all six stubs (`test rust`, `build release|deploy|nif|firmware`, `db proxy` -- rc 3 with identical text), `db codegen` bare (rc 1), `test suite bogus` (rc 1), `cv warp` (rc 1). Eleven identical pairs plus the three refusal pairs.

## Usage-path probes

| Probe                    | Old        | New        | Note                                                          |
| ------------------------ | ---------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| bare `test`              | topic rc 0 | topic rc 0 | Baize's shape preserved (Laksa's rc-2 is Laksa's ruling)      |
| bare `db`/`cv`/`perf`/`build`/`docs` | topic rc 0 | topic rc 0 | authored topics on the new side (re-rendered as markdown -- same content, not byte-compared) |
| bare `check`             | topic rc 0 | usage rc 1 | DELIBERATE: devbin's bare-gate ruling -- a gate command exiting 0 having run nothing is a false green (`check && deploy` deploys). The topic lives at `baize help check`. Established at Laksa; recorded here explicitly. |
| `check -h`               | topic rc 0 | usage line rc 0 | same ruling's -h face; full topic at `help check`         |
| `fmt --check` (old only) | rc 0       | --         | retired into `check format` (D21) -- probed rc 0 old, and `check format` rc 0 new: same command, same verdict |
| `version sync` / `check` | --         | rc 0       | surface additions; no sidecars, both report and change nothing |

## Deliberate differences, each with an owner

1. **fmt surface** (D21, fleet): bare `fmt` -> usage rc 1; `fmt elixir` / `fmt all` format; `fmt --check` retired into `check format` (probed equivalent above). **`fmt md` DISABLED in config** -- Baize's own authored ruling ("do not add without a ruling") encoded as `enabled: false`; the arm refuses by name with the config path.
2. **bare `check` exits 1** (and `check -h` prints a usage line, not the topic) -- devbin's bare-gate false-green ruling, uniform across the fleet.
3. **`check all` order**: coverage identical (six gates); declared rows run first. Baize's old order had no authored toolchain-first ruling (unlike Laksa), so the slot shuffle is cosmetic and recorded, not preserved.
4. **`test all` accepts the gate wrapper flags** (--purge/--purge-only/--allow-empty), fanned to the SEALED runners only -- hv's fleet ruling 2026-08-09; shell is deliberately unsealed and rust is a stub, so neither has a seal family for the flags to act on. `--full` and the refusal of everything else stand.
5. **One promotion the old runner did not make**: a Result trailer counting zero executed now promotes (the old runner only promoted the no-Result case). Issue-0006 doctrine; stated in the test topic.
6. **Shared options consumed anywhere in argv** (old scoped them pre-command in effect). Exposure: no bz.* task declares `--env`/`--json`/`--iex` switches. Documented in the cli topic.
7. **Seal suffix family**: `<stamp>.MIX.*` / `<stamp>.CREDO.*` vs the old lowercase. LATEST pointer NAMES unchanged. Old lowercase runs become purge-invisible orphans at the switch -- hand-clean via case-sensitive `find -name`, per protocol.
8. **Surface additions**: `version sync`/`version check` (no-ops here), sealed check verdicts under `tmp/check/`, the Devbin command group.

## Project dirt, surfaced (hv to note)

`db reset` runs the root `mix setup` alias -- whose deprecated `mix cmd --app` spelling `db setup` deliberately avoids and documents avoiding. CARRIED VERBATIM in cmd/db (a faithful shadow, with the dirt named in its header); aligning reset with setup's direct form is a one-line Baize-side fix awaiting its own ruling.

## What this migration found in devbin (AC-11.11 feed)

- **Issue 0007** (new): the gate usage lines (`usage: baize fmt <elixir|rust|swift|md|all>`, `check <...clippy...>`) list the RAW CATALOGUE, not the active set -- three advertised fmt arms refuse here. The refusals themselves are precise and the generated global help is right; only gatecmd's usage strings read the catalogue. Filed with three options (dispatcher export / gatecmd re-derivation / decline) rather than patched mid-migration -- the fix touches the D11 activation seam.
- **The negative data point for the toolchain design call**: Baize has NO Dockerfile, no fly.toml, no image ARGs -- the "Dockerfile arm" is a two-of-four corpus pattern (Conflab, Laksa), not a norm. Lamplight will settle the count.

## The switch-day map (AC-11.20/21, for hv's go)

- `bin/baize` -> symlink to devbin; `bin/bz` is ALREADY a symlink to `baize` and rides unchanged (chains through).
- `bin/cli` and `bin/repl` exec `baize_cli`/`baize_repl` DIRECTLY -- retargeted in the switch commit to route through `bin/baize`.
- `test/shell/helpers_test.sh` sources `bin/baize_helpers` (its subject): in the switch commit its source line moves to the vendored `bin/.devbin/lib/{helpers,runlog}` (`init_run_colors` -> `init_colors`, grammar globals -> `grammar_for`), keeping the project's local gate on the machinery its verdicts rest on; `test shell` re-runs green post-switch as part of the verification.
- The 22 `baize_*` files delete; old lowercase seals hand-cleaned case-sensitively.

## Not probed at depth, and why

Execution of `server` (agent-banned -- and the ban itself verified by design: the guard reads CLAUDECODE/CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, exported into this shell), `iex`, `repl`, `cli` (interactive; dispatch + -h verified), `publish` (builds PDFs into docs/, mutating; dispatch + guard verified), `cv`/`perf` execution (need local fixtures / minutes of pipeline; the caller-CWD absolutising logic is ported verbatim and `cv` misuse paths probed), `db setup/migrate/codegen/reset/seed` (database mutations), `docs agents/index/completions` (regenerate tracked artifacts), `fmt elixir` (tree mutation; its check twin probed).

## Verdict

Every command the old launcher offered exists under the same name and dispatches. The gates that measure the project measured IDENTICAL sets with identical verdicts on both sides -- 29 marker tests, 330 credo files / 1908 mods-funs, 64 shell assertions, six check gates, four critic languages -- with eleven byte-identical outputs and three byte-identical refusals. No red exists on either side today (the toolchain sweep was a verified no-op). The deliberate differences are enumerated with owners; the one piece of project dirt is carried loudly. This is the evidence step 5 (the switch) is authorised over -- pending hv's explicit per-project go.
